arxiv-2010-03301.title: On the cohomology of reciprocity sheaves Thanks: F.B. is supported by the PRIN “Geometric, Algebraic and Analytic Methods in Arithmetic” and is a member of the INdAM group GNSAGA. K.R. was supported by the DFG Heisenberg Grant RU 1412/2-2. S.S. is supported by the JSPS KAKENHI Grant (20H01791).
arxiv-2010-03301.creator: Federico Binda, Kay Rülling, and Shuji Saito
arxiv-2010-03301.description: Abstract . In this paper we show the existence of an action of Chow correspondences on the cohomology of reciprocity sheaves. In order to do so, we prove a number of structural results, such as a projective bundle formula, a blow-up formula, a Gysin sequence, and the existence of proper pushforward.

arxiv-2105-05832.title: Sample-efficient device-independent quantum state verification and certification
arxiv-2105-05832.creator: Aleksandra Gočanin, Ivan Šupić, Borivoje Dakić
arxiv-2105-05832.description: Abstract Authentication of quantum sources is a crucial task in building reliable and efficient protocols for quantum-information processing. Steady progress vis-à-vis verification of quantum devices in the scenario with fully characterized measurement devices has been observed in recent years. When it comes to the scenario with uncharacterized measurements, the so-called black-box scenario, practical verification methods are still rather scarce.

arxiv-2105-08116.title: A Neat Linked Queue with the Rear Blank Node
arxiv-2105-08116.creator: Xie Xie xiexiexx@gmail.com
arxiv-2105-08116.description: Abstract We introduce a very simple queue implementation with the singly linked list. With the help of the rear blank node instead of the usual header node, we avoid additional check steps for the dequeue operation in the traditional implementations existing for many decades.

arxiv-2201-09978.title: An empirical model for feedforward control of laser powder bed fusion
arxiv-2201-09978.creator: Aleksandr Shkoruta, Bumsoo Park, Sandipan Mishra
arxiv-2201-09978.description: Abstract Highlights 1. Laser scanning of narrow features in LPBF parts results in predictable changes in melt pool geometry as observed in coaxial melt pool images. 2. An empirical model of this geometry-related behavior, validated on different geometries, is presented. 3. A model-based feedforward controller is designed to correct for this behavior.

arxiv-2206-06244.title: Benefits and Limitations of Simplified Transient Gas Flow Formulations
arxiv-2206-06244.creator: Felix Hennings
arxiv-2206-06244.description: Abstract Although intensively studied in recent years, the optimization of the transient (time-dependent) control of large real-world gas networks is still out of reach for current state-of-the-art approaches. For this reason, we present further simplifications of the commonly used model, which lead to a linear description of the gas flow on pipelines.

arxiv-2209-01985.title: Small Area Estimation of Inequality Measures using Mixtures of Beta
arxiv-2209-01985.creator: Silvia De Nicolò, Maria Rosaria Ferrante, Silvia Pacei
arxiv-2209-01985.description: Abstract Economic inequalities referring to specific regions are crucial in deepening spatial heterogeneity. Income surveys are generally planned to produce reliable estimates at countries or macroregion levels, thus we implement a small area model for a set of inequality measures (Gini, Relative Theil and Atkinson indexes) to obtain reliable microregion estimates.

arxiv-2305-06714.title: Factorization systems and double categories
arxiv-2305-06714.creator: Miloslav Štěpán
arxiv-2305-06714.description: Abstract . We show that factorization systems, both strict and orthogonal, can be equivalently described as double categories satisfying certain properties. This provides conceptual reasons for why the category of sets and partial maps or the category of small categories and cofunctors admit orthogonal factorization systems.

arxiv-2308-04692.title: Conformal geodesics and the evolution of spacetimes with positive Cosmological constant
arxiv-2308-04692.creator: Marica Minucci
arxiv-2308-04692.description: Abstract This article provides a discussion on the construction of conformal Gaussian gauge systems to study the evolution of solutions to the Einstein field equations with positive Cosmological constant. This is done by means of a gauge based on the properties of conformal geodesics.

arxiv-2409-03880.title: Multi-color solitons and frequency combs in microresonators
arxiv-2409-03880.creator: Curtis R. Menyuk, 1,* Pradyoth Shandilya, 1 Logan Courtright, 1 Grégory Moille, 2,3 and Kartik Srinivasan 2,3
arxiv-2409-03880.description: Abstract Multi-color solitons that are parametrically created in dual-pumped microresonators generate interleaved frequency combs that can be used to obtain combs at new frequencies and when synchronized can be used for low-noise microwave generation and potentially as an element in a chip-scale clockwork.

arxiv-2511-12725.title: Convolutional Model Trees
arxiv-2511-12725.creator: William Ward Armstrong
arxiv-2511-12725.description: Abstract A method for creating a forest of model trees to fit samples of a function defined on images is described in several steps: down-sampling the images, determining a tree’s hyperplanes, applying convolutions to the hyperplanes to handle small distortions of training images, and creating forests of model trees to increase accuracy and achieve a smooth fit.

arxiv-2604-13936.title: Topological markers for a one-dimensional fermionic chain coupled to a single-mode cavity
arxiv-2604-13936.creator: Anna Ritz-Zwilling, Olesia Dmytruk

pmc-11312003.title: Spatial Analysis of Health System Factors in Infectious Disease Management: Lessons Learned from the COVID-19 Pandemic in Korea
pmc-11312003.creator: Jeongwook Lee, SangA Lee, Andrea Tittarelli
pmc-11312003.description: Infectious disease outbreaks present ongoing and substantial challenges to health systems at local, national, and global levels, testing their preparedness, response capabilities, and resilience. This study aimed to identify and analyze critical health system-level factors that influence infection outbreaks, focusing on the experience of the COVID-19 pandemic in Korea.

pmc-11430950.title: Robot-Assisted Extravesical Ureteral Reimplantation (REVUR) in Pediatric Patients: A New Standard of Treatment for Patients with VUR—A Narrative Review
pmc-11430950.creator: Ciro Esposito, Claudia Di Mento, Mariapina Cerulo, Fulvia Del Conte, Francesco Tedesco, Vincenzo Coppola, Annalisa Chiodi, Giorgia Esposito, Leonardo Continisio, Marco Castagnetti, Maria Escolino, Zenon Pogorelić
pmc-11430950.description: Robot-assisted extravesical ureteral reimplantation (REVUR) was described for the first time in 2004. Since then, the surgical approach of vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) has changed dramatically. The benefits of this technique are great when compared to the laparoscopic or traditional open approaches. A literature search of PubMed was performed to identify articles covering any aspect of REVUR in the pediatric population.

pmc-12470719.title: Unraveling Resistance in Lung Cancer Immunotherapy: Clinical Milestones, Mechanistic Insights, and Future Strategies
pmc-12470719.creator: Maria Vitale, Raffaella Pagliaro, Giuseppe Viscardi, Lucio Pastore, Giuseppe Castaldo, Fabio Perrotta, Susan F Campbell, Andrea Bianco, Filippo Scialò, Atsushi Matsuzawa
pmc-12470719.description: Over the last decade, immunotherapy has revolutionized lung cancer treatments, particularly in non-small cell lung cancer, where immune checkpoint inhibitors have achieved significant clinical success. However, high percentages of patients do not respond initially or eventually develop a resistance to these therapies.

pmc-12555537.title: Evaluating the Healthy Neighbourhood Approach in Rotterdam
pmc-12555537.creator: EE De Vries, S Bom, Y Sebaihi, I Merkelbach
pmc-12555537.description: BackgroundHealth information does not reach all communities of Rotterdam equally. In response, the municipal health service Rotterdam-Rijnmond (GGD) developed “The Healthy Neighbourhood approach” (HNA), a culturally sensitive, outreach-based program aimed at strengthening health literacy and reducing health inequalities. This intervention is currently being implemented in two vulnerable neighbourhoods in Rotterdam.

pmc-13251245.title: The impact of emergency intubation on surgical outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection AADA (DeBakey I). Is a prompt treatment justified?
pmc-13251245.creator: Morsi Arar, Erik Beckmann, Andreas Martens, Florian Helms, Heike Krueger, Linda Rudolph, Ezin Deniz, Stefan Todorov, Jan Schmitto, Bastian Schmack, Arjang Ruhparwar, Malakh Shrestha, Tim Kaufeld
pmc-13251245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAn acute aortic dissection Stanford type A (AADA) is a life-threatening disease and one of the urgent emergencies in cardiovascular surgery. Furthermore, mortality increases when further risk factors like malperfusion, cardiac tamponade or preoperative cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) occur.

pmc-13291115.title: Microbial induced calcium carbonate precipitation under extreme environmental conditions: impacts on biomineralization process and mechanical performance of concrete
pmc-13291115.creator: Mai M. Abdelwahed, Amany M. Reyad, Ahmed. Abd-Alazim, Gehad Mokhtar

pmc-13343793.title: Opinions of speech-language-hearing pathologists and students on evidence-based practice: a systematic review
pmc-13343793.creator: Samara Fernandes da Silva Souza, Allya Francisca Marques Borges, Ramon Cipriano Pacheco de Araújo, Denise da Silva Medeiros, Suzanne Bettega Almeida, Cristiano Miranda de Araujo, Hipólito Virgílio Magalhães, Karinna Veríssimo Meira Taveira, Samara Fernandes da Silva Souza, Allya Francisca Marques Bo
pmc-13343793.description: PurposeTo synthesize evidence on the knowledge, skills, attitudes, behaviors, and barriers reported by speech-language-hearing pathologists and students regarding evidence-based practice (EBP).Research strategyThis systematic review searches the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, LILACS, SciELO, and LIVIVO databases and grey literature.

pmc-13458095.title: Temporal distribution of acute kidney injury–related hospitalizations after initiation of sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors: A nationwide claims database analysis in older adults with an independent complementary single‐center eGFR analysis
pmc-13458095.creator: Kazuya Hiura, Ayana Tatsuno, Yamato Noto, Ryosuke Wakamatsu, Masayuki Sakunami, Ryu Kobayashi, Miki Yamashita
pmc-13458095.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aims/IntroductionSodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce the risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). However, an initial decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) may occur after initiation, and factors associated with sustained early eGFR decline remain unclear. We evaluated the temporal distribution of AKI‐related hospitalizations in older adults using claims data and, in an independent single‐center cohort, factors associated with sustained early eGFR decline.Materials and MethodsA Japanese nationwide claims database identified patients aged ≥75 years emergently hospitalized with AKI after SGLT2i initiation.

pmc-13563630.title: Hydrolysis-Driven Compositional Modification of Flavonoids in the Aerial Parts of Lespedeza cyrtobotrya Miq. and Its Impact on Monoamine Oxidase A Inhibitory Activity
pmc-13563630.creator: Hyoung-Geun Kim, Su-Ah Lee, Ji-Hong Kim, Su-Yeon Lee, Jongmin Ahn, Sei-Ryang Oh, Dongho Lee, Sung-Kyun Ko, Hyung Won Ryu
pmc-13563630.description: This study was conducted to investigate processing-induced compositional modification of flavonoids in Lespedeza cyrtobotrya and its impact on food-relevant bioactivity using a quantitative and validated analytical approach. Extracts, fractions, and isolated compounds from the aerial parts were systematically evaluated for monoamine oxidase inhibitory activity as a functional indicator.

pmc-13677047.title: Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca2+‐CaMKK2‐AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD
pmc-13677047.creator: Xiang Wei, Li Lin, Xiuyun Wang, Hui Du, Menglong Zhang, Kechao Tang, Han Gao, Xinrui Xie, Jingya Gao, Xu Wang, Zhenglin Wang, Siwei Huang, Lei Zhang, Fang Gu, Gong‐Hong Wei, Yinliang Qi, Wei Chen, Yongsheng Chang, Huabing Zhang
pmc-13677047.description: Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one‐third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb‐associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (db/db, ob/ob, HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes in vitro.
